approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from a bounded, score-ranked population of accepted molecules. It draws a first parent from weighted score bands and either mutates that molecule or crosses it with a separately drawn, distinct partner. Crossover usually keeps the larger fragment of the first parent and the smaller fragment of the partner, with an optional finishing mutation. Ordinary mutation can continue for several steps; direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Stable canonical identity and duplicate checks form a fresh proposal pool. A Gaussian process fitted to all accepted scores uses counts of local molecular environments and correlated posterior draws to select evaluations. Accepted offspring update both the predictive archive and the score-greedy breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove rank preference only when choosing the crossover partner. Keep precisely the partners the original law could select, but choose uniformly among them; every first-parent request keeps its original weighted rule. Earlier siblings removed weights in both roles, expanded eligibility to all live survivors, balanced first-parent schedules, or favored chemically similar partners. None isolated this partner-only weight contribution on the current Parent. The hypothesis is that flattening partner probabilities weakens the scored graft-source distribution and may lower final best scores despite broader partner use. This is a conditional contribution control, with the first-parent law and graph construction preserved.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent concentrates score-rank probability in two chemically asymmetric source roles, but current evidence has not localized which role benefits from that concentration. The actual summary.json and run.log for all three Parent replicas n-62daf219c70a report complete successful five-task panels, macro mean 0.5956696497334577 and population SD 0.02659287062806747. A read-only reconstruction of all fifteen Parent task logs, using chronological accepted training records and checking every actual parent identity, score, origin and rank, finds 75961 first requests and 34334 actual crossover-partner requests. All 34334 partner states differ from uniformity on the exact original support; 702 exclusions empty one original band, and none invokes the whole no-group fallback. On these actual partner states the hypothetical uniform law has mean total-variation distance 0.41303181345456674 from the original law, expected topness 0.7495348330864349 versus 0.8814935586905972, and expected real parent score 0.4155250445737675 versus 0.4421389892341994. These are probability integrals on observed states, not generated alternate offspring or a score estimate for a new run. The audit is .slots/round-0023-slot-3/parent_role_opportunity.json. The earlier same-Parent original-support removal n-f30747ffdbf8 changed both roles, preserved support in all 108254 requests, changed 103018 coupled parent identities and reached 4020 accepted products; it lost paired macro mean 0.05700288256234002. Its current catalog interpretation supports the joint all-role within-support weight contribution only. Strict parent beats nevertheless rose from 629 to 936 while mean absolute offspring score fell from 0.385256 to 0.321688. The broader uniform-live sibling n-a56491c332aa additionally changed support and lost 0.04599801243765703. The prospective first-parent scheduler n-f68f386d4d9d retained marginal rank weights, increased coverage and local wins, yet lost 0.04216145214436932. Historical similarity-weighted partners n-a20706504e8f, core balancing n-69c038cb49ac and success credit n-030a6ccbba7c also have adverse measured means on their older binary-posterior Parent; they test different laws and their current catalog contribution remains unresolved. None answers the frozen partner-only question. The limiting uncertainty is productive graft-source allocation, not established harm from rank preference or proof that uniformity is better.
hypothesis: Remove nonuniform score-rank weighting only from actual crossover-partner requests, choosing uniformly from the increasing-rank union of the inherited positive-probability groups after original first-parent exclusion and empty-group fallback; keep the original band draw passive for that role and preserve every first-parent request under its original weighted band and within-band law.

finding_summary.headline: Crossover-partner rank weights contribute: their removal lowers mean final Top-1 by 0.051808
finding_summary.insights:
The score-ranked crossover partner has positive conditional value even when the first-parent rule and eligible partner set are preserved. Earlier removal in both roles could not localize that value; this control answers the partner question. It leaves first-parent contribution, support-only value and the value of the complete graph-evolution system open. Shared-baseline results cannot be added or subtracted into those answers.

More local success did not mean better search. Strict best-parent wins rose from 629 to 702, accepted offspring later reused rose from 2,401 to 2,619, and incumbent advances rose from 258 to 265. But the generating reference weakened: mean best-parent score fell from 0.470456 to 0.386162, mean offspring score fell from 0.385256 to 0.325006, and the average positive incumbent increment fell from 0.022510 to 0.018983. These results rule out treating local win counts, reuse or lower dispersion as sufficient evidence of productive exploration.

The molecular assessment describes substantial aromatic, amine and carbonyl chemistry, including a comparatively conventional nitrile ketone in the improved zaleplon run. The largest losses include failure to recover the Parent’s compact high-scoring decoration-hopping arrangement, while much larger decorated structures, reactive nitrogen/oxygen–halogen bonds, difficult ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry persist. Those associations suggest a gap in useful feasible alternatives, but neither the cleaner counterexample nor the liabilities identify the chemical cause of the loss. Partner identities, subsequent graph randomness and adaptive feedback remain inseparable parts of this measured total effect.
finding_summary.results:
All 75,472 first-parent draws retained the original rule. Partner selection preserved exactly the original eligible identities but changed 32,483 of 34,304 choices when replayed against the inherited choice from the same random state. On those same populations, expected partner score fell from 0.365128 to 0.342519. Changed choices reached 1,439 accepted crossover offspring; 797 of those offspring later bred. Greedy survival, complete accepted-score learning and all 435 full candidate-pool selections remained active.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.543862, a paired change of -0.051808 against the registered 0.002 scale. Seed-average changes were -0.087771, -0.005118 and -0.062534. Eleven of fifteen task/seed endpoints declined; zaleplon seed 0, median similarity seeds 1 and 2, and sitagliptin seed 1 improved. Task means rose for zaleplon and median similarity but fell for decoration hopping, docking and sitagliptin. Seed-average population deviation fell from 0.026593 to 0.008407. Every task completed its full oracle budget.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic output mixes a plausible nitrile ketone and aryl amines with reactive halogen bonds and difficult polycycles
molecular.overall_character: This assessment names n-ee95752352ec and compares its actual output with code Parent n-62daf219c70a. All 15 Child Search trajectories and all 15 published Parent trajectories were present and read in full. Each task has 900 records, including 870 optimizer proposals, across seeds 0, 1 and 2; no task lacks trajectories. The request reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, with matched seeds 0, 1 and 2 and no profile mismatches. The current comparison is therefore complete under the supplied epoch-1 profile, batch size 10 and 300 observations per task/seed. The historical gap source n-c55c3d520a2c and its carried-forward n-62daf219c70a report were read through context.evidence_index; that earlier same-code baseline reproduction had profile-mismatched pairing and is retained only as gap provenance, not another matched replicate. The output comprises nitrile-substituted fused heteroaromatic ketones and amides, extended nitrogen-rich diones, aryl/aliphatic amines, bridged nitrogen-carbonyl systems, and fluorinated diones with unusual nitrogen substitution. Child ring-closure-string incidence is 0.9644 to 0.9862 and aromatic-string incidence is 0.9586 to 0.9816. Those are molecule-level text-feature rates, not fractions of aromatic atoms or independent scaffolds. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidence are 0.0 on every task; protonatable amines and potentially stereogenic centres nevertheless occur. All optimizer records in both panels parsed with the locally available RDKit. Heavy-atom counts, ring sizes and bond counts below were derived from those supplied strings; graph perception does not establish realizable geometry, a synthesis, configurational stability or activity. The inventory and file hashes are recorded in .slots/round-0023-slot-3/molecular/trajectory_inventory.json. There is substantial chemistry across tasks and seeds, but leading examples within a seed repeatedly retain the same families. The cleaner ketone leader and recognizable cyclic amines are counterexamples to universal chemical implausibility; O-halogen and N-halogen bonds, difficult small-ring fusions, large decorated frameworks and unspecified stereochemistry justify the weaker overall quality judgement. Digest final_molecules are late seed-2 proposals, not each seed's best retained molecule. Parent structures are described by their authoritative seed/evaluation positions; cited_smiles contains only Child molecules admitted by the trusted request. These are conditional chemistry associations, with no attribution to a search component, mechanism-activation decision or eligibility judgement.

per_task.generated_character: Optimizer proposals have median 25 heavy atoms and median 3 perceived rings; mean SMILES length is 42.5. The seed-0 leader at evaluation 129 has 24 heavy atoms: a methoxy/methyl/nitrile-substituted benzimidazole with a ketone linking it to a methylphenylmethyl group. Its ordinary N-H, nitrile, ether and ketone bonding makes it a more recognizable synthetic target than many nearby alternatives. Seed 1 evaluation 119 instead has 23 heavy atoms and a carbonyl-linked aza-aromatic unit attached to a partly unsaturated NH ring system; perceived cycles include a seven-membered ring. Seed 2 evaluation 203 has 26 heavy atoms, a methyl thioether, an N-N-containing fused four-membered thione ring and an aryl urea-like carbonyl linkage. Thus neither the pooled leading family nor its comparatively conventional bonding represents all seeds. The Parent leaders at evaluations 289, 293 and 294 retain indole-like aromatic frameworks but carry N-Cl or N-F substitution, with cumulene, N-hydroxy amide or vicinal-diketone functionality. Child N-halogen incidence is 81 of 870 optimizer molecules, versus 445 of 870 for the Parent; this is a local bond-inventory change, not proof of generally improved chemistry.
liabilities: Near-leading amides contain N-Cl or N-F, and other high variants combine nitrogen-sulfur attachments with aromatic carbonyl frameworks. These bonds differ chemically from ordinary aryl C-halogen substitution.
The seed-2 four-membered N-N/thione fusion and seed-1 unusual ring junctions require geometry and synthesis scrutiny; parsing and score do not establish their accessibility.
Much larger aromatic dimers and very small fragments remain in the scored output despite poor scores.
missing_features: Consistently plausible alternatives to the fused N-N/thione and unusual aza-ring families are not demonstrated at the cleaner seed-0 leader's score. Conventional N-H heteroaromatic chemistry is already attainable, so it is not a missing capability in absolute terms.

Leading alternatives usually preserve a seed-specific fused aromatic/carbonyl organization. The record does not demonstrate broad coverage of independent, feasible connectivities that retain that favorable arrangement.
Potential saturated-ring stereochemistry in the seed-1 family remains unspecified; the achiral-looking seed-0 leader is an explicit exception to a universal stereochemical deficiency.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145, while the seed-0 nitrile/benzyl-ketone leader reaches 0.5188745216627708. A larger coupled aromatic-amide proposal at seed 0 evaluation 24 scores only 3.5758235031768006e-16, and ethene at seed 1 evaluation 196 scores 0.0. The visible reward therefore concerns a compact combined aromatic/polar arrangement, not aromatic content or size alone. A neighboring N-chloro amide at seed 0 evaluation 195 scores 0.5108921546316982, so high scores tolerate a reactive nitrogen environment but the best Child example does not require it. The late seed-2 thione/azaaryl-urea variant at evaluation 300 scores 0.37081201154324345, below that seed's best. Child best observed scores on seeds 0, 1 and 2 are 0.5188745216627708, 0.4239904333396317, 0.4254027310763201; the published Parent values in the same order are 0.39405142067435733, 0.47411701813450596, 0.438972502037081. The opposite seed-level directions and different skeletons do not identify a unique missing pharmacophore or a causal chemical mediator.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest typical Child output: median 41 heavy atoms versus the Parent's 33, with mean SMILES length 78.2 and maximum length 206. Child leaders on seeds 0, 1 and 2 have 57, 48 and 50 heavy atoms, whereas the corresponding Parent leaders have 30, 32 and 37. The seed-0 leader at evaluation 215 is a heavily decorated nitrogen-rich aromatic dione with polyene chains, ethers and fluorinated ester-bearing substituents. Seed 1 evaluation 300 combines several aza-aromatic rings and a dione with carbonyl/imine linkers and a bromochlorophenyl appendage. Seed 2 evaluation 232 retains a fused nitrogen-rich dione, an aza-aryl/fluorophenyl region and an extended unsaturated ether-containing side chain, with three O-Br bonds. These are elaborate ring-containing molecules rather than simple fragments, but the reactive attachments and synthetic complexity make feasibility questionable. The compact Parent seed-0 leader at evaluation 281 also has an O-F liability, so its more favorable score does not establish an intrinsically safe or synthesis-ready template.
liabilities: O-halogen bonds occur in 224 of 870 Child optimizer molecules versus 89 of 870 Parent molecules. The seed-2 leader specifically uses hypobromite-like O-Br connectivity, rather than ordinary carbon-bound bromine.

Long decorated unsaturated chains, multiple carbonyl/imine functions and densely linked heterocycles create substantial synthetic and stability questions; carbon-bound halogens alone do not explain these concerns.
The seed-2 tied neighborhood retains reactive attachments, while the score floor of 0.5 for tiny fragments does not imply useful molecular chemistry.
missing_features: The Child leaders lack a compact, plausibly accessible realization of the favorable linked nitrogen-heterocycle arrangement at the Parent seed-0 score. Ring formation and nitrogen-carbonyl chemistry are abundant; adding more rings is not supported as the missing feature.
Stable peripheral replacements that preserve useful functional-group relationships while reducing O-halogen and unsaturated-chain liabilities are not established at the leading Child score.
Stereochemical definition at substituted side-chain centres and geometric definition of the cited polyenes are absent from the representative SMILES.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.548381482770623; an ethoxyamino fluorophenyl fragment at seed 0 evaluation 15 scores 0.5044095599259194, and ethene at seed 2 evaluation 271 sits at 0.5. The higher Child scores occur with combined heterocyclic assemblies. Seed-2 evaluations 232, 266 and 295 all score 0.6029411764705882 despite peripheral changes including added chlorine and altered terminal bromine connectivity. These ties show that additional decoration does not necessarily improve score; they do not isolate any one O-Br bond as necessary or dispensable. Child best observed scores on seeds 0, 1 and 2 are 0.5963349658253054, 0.600329851566795, 0.6029411764705882; the published Parent values in the same order are 0.8561477222467935, 0.6248206599713055, 0.6178024026512013. The larger Child leaders never reproduce the compact Parent seed-0 arrangement's supplied score. This is a missing observed chemical outcome, not evidence that shrinking arbitrary molecules or copying a named objective's scaffold would work.

per_task.generated_character: The Child produces substantial aryl/aliphatic-amine molecules, with median 34 heavy atoms versus the Parent's 31 and mean SMILES length 71.7. Seed 1 evaluation 292 has 31 heavy atoms: an aminomethyl substituent, a tertiary azetidine nitrogen, a bromophenol ring and a fluorinated benzofused unsaturated ether region. Seed 0 evaluation 281 has 32 heavy atoms with primary/secondary amines, substituted aryl groups, a cyclohexene and an unusual methylene-double-bonded sulfur bearing additional carbon substituents. Seed 2 evaluation 283 has 34 heavy atoms and connects an aryl thioether/biphenyl region to substituted azetidine and pyrrolidine rings. Basic nitrogen centres and aromatic surface are clearly present. The Parent leaders are a flexible tertiary arylalkyl amine at seed 0 evaluation 284 and recognizable pyrrolidine-containing frameworks at seed 1 evaluation 261 and seed 2 evaluation 241. Ordinary cyclic amines can be plausible synthetic units; the Child's larger and more stereochemically complex combinations are not thereby validated.
liabilities: The seed-0 leader has an unusual tetravalent sulfur environment, while several saturated ring junctions and heavily substituted small rings require stereochemical and conformational checking.

Halogen-string incidence is 0.9885. Substantial aryl halogen loading and carbon-bound halogens near amine-containing rings coexist with hydrophobic segments; their scores do not establish favorable solubility, stability or selectivity.

Azetidines and pyrrolidines themselves are not evidence of impossible chemistry. The concern is the complete substitution and ring arrangement, especially when its stereochemical identity is unspecified.
missing_features: Explicit stereochemical identity is missing for the leading substituted saturated-ring, benzylic and branched centres. RDKit finds unassigned potential centres in 854 of 870 Child optimizer molecules; this is a graph-level observation, not an experimentally stable stereoisomer count.

A consistently accessible arrangement of the already-present amines and aryl groups at the Parent outcomes is not demonstrated. The trajectory cannot identify a unique absent substituent or justify simply adding another basic nitrogen.
Relevant protonation and conformational states are not specified by the neutral SMILES. Zero charge-string incidence is not evidence that the molecules lack protonatable centres.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: A small dichlorophenyl sulfone at seed 2 evaluation 20 scores 0.00032141189568530486, and an alkyl N-sulfonyl compound at seed 0 evaluation 69 scores 0.00048480624806484054. The strongest Child examples combine accessible aliphatic amines with larger aryl regions. At seed 1, replacing the leader's primary aminomethyl branch with fluorine in evaluation 272 still gives 0.9881143442283419 while retaining the cyclic tertiary amine. Thus an additional primary amine is not necessary for a near-leading score in this family. A simpler sulfur-containing aryl/cycloalkenyl amine at seed 0 evaluation 298 scores 0.9256520411115274 without the unusual sulfur environment of that seed's leader. Child best observed scores on seeds 0, 1 and 2 are 0.9304234123632887, 0.9903644142812332, 0.8902313197553174; the published Parent values in the same order are 0.9999989177995104, 0.9969753164881906, 0.9999934235240012. These supplied scores support a conditional association with amine/aryl presentation, not a measured binding affinity, a claim about protonation state, or proof that maximal size, sulfur complexity or halogen loading is required.

per_task.generated_character: The typical Child proposal has 32 heavy atoms and 5 perceived rings, compared with Parent medians of 30 heavy atoms and 5 rings; mean SMILES length is 55.6. Seed 0 evaluation 257 has 28 heavy atoms and a densely connected aza-aromatic and N-methyl dicarbonyl framework, including perceived eight- and nine-membered cycles. Seed 1 evaluation 272 has 35 heavy atoms with phenyl, ethoxy-substituted aza-aromatic and partially unsaturated nitrogen-ring regions, linked to N-methyl carbonyl groups. Its perceived rings include an oxygen-containing four-membered fusion and larger nitrogen-carbonyl cycles. Seed 2 evaluation 241 also has 35 heavy atoms, combining propyl/ethoxy aza-aromatic and phenyl regions with a hydroxylated, nitrogen-containing dicarbonyl ring. The Parent leaders likewise combine aza-aryl and bridged nitrogen-carbonyl chemistry, but with different ring connectivity. Halogen incidence is relatively low at 0.1494 and cumulated-double-bond-string incidence is 0.0: the main concern here is topology and identity, not an absence of carbonyls or a universal reactive-halogen motif.
liabilities: Medium-ring bridges, multiple ring junctions and the seed-1 oxygen-containing four-membered fusion raise practical synthesis and geometry questions.
Near-leading O-F substitution introduces a reactivity concern without improving its cited hydroxyl analogue's score.
Potential stereogenic saturated centres remain unspecified even though recognizable amide, ether and aza-aromatic functions are present.
missing_features: The leading bridged and fused arrangements lack demonstrated accessible geometry and specified stereochemistry. Simpler relatives occur at nearby scores, so the gap is consistent feasible alternatives rather than an inability to change connectivity.

Independent, plausibly synthesizable frameworks preserving the favorable aryl/nitrogen-carbonyl organization are not established broadly among the leaders; high ring count does not answer this coverage question.

Neither additional halogens nor a particular oxygen atom is shown to be the missing feature: the hydroxyl/O-F comparison and tolerated linker changes point to the combined framework rather than one uniquely required local bond.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329. An isolated ethoxy aza-aromatic/oxygen-ring fragment at seed 1 evaluation 243 scores 0.09369968652822305, and methane at seed 1 evaluation 161 scores 0.0; higher scores occur for combined aryl and nitrogen-carbonyl frameworks. Inserting a methylene before the pendant aza-aromatic region at seed 1 evaluation 241 gives 0.233131210087964, close to that seed's 0.23473509048594163 leader. The seed-2 hydroxyl-containing leader scores 0.23410836872198745; its O-F replacement at evaluation 299 scores 0.2304597033169082. This close pair provides a direct counterexample to assuming the reactive O-F bond improves the family. A less aromatic, differently connected 32-heavy-atom relative at evaluation 285 still scores 0.23100354985671173, showing that useful nearby topology alternatives already occur. Child best observed scores on seeds 0, 1 and 2 are 0.2211950795406116, 0.23473509048594163, 0.23410836872198745; the published Parent values in the same order are 0.2258403994203931, 0.2214095461892601, 0.22600312875247064. These small local differences do not reveal an exact absent target pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: Child proposals have median 28 heavy atoms versus the Parent's 27, and mean SMILES length 53.4. The seed-2 leader at evaluation 224 has 28 heavy atoms: an aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen dione ring attached to a phenyl ring with a fluoroacetyl group and an O-linked nitrogen bearing two fluorines; the dione ring has another N-F bond. Seed 1 evaluation 299 has 29 heavy atoms and combines a substituted cyclopropene, an oxygen-containing four-membered ring within a fused assembly, hydroxyl substitution and two N-F bonds on the dione region. Seed 0 evaluation 191 has 28 heavy atoms and an N-fluorinated fused dione with a bridged aryl/alkyl region, carbon-bound fluorine and a methyl ester. N-halogen bonds occur in 700 of 870 Child optimizer molecules, versus 476 of 870 Parent molecules. The Parent seed-2 leader at evaluation 273 instead combined a nitrogen imino/carbonyl ring with a small cyclic cumulene and had no N-F bond. That particular Parent liability is not the Child leading motif, but the Child's unusual N-fluorination and ring chemistry do not establish improved feasibility.
liabilities: N-F bonds on carbonyl-adjacent ring nitrogens and on O-linked nitrogen are unlike ordinary medicinal C-F substitution and create local reactivity concerns.
Cyclopropene substitution, fused oxygen-containing four-membered rings and larger aromatic-labelled nitrogen rings require geometry and synthetic scrutiny; no score supplies that validation.
The highly substituted seed-1 saturated centres lack stereochemical assignments, while terminal elaborations of the seed-2 leader can lose substantial score.
missing_features: The highest Child examples do not demonstrate ordinary, stable nitrogen substitution while retaining their favorable compact fluorinated/carbonyl organization. Conventional carbon-bound fluorine exists already; the missing consistency concerns local bonding, not fluorination itself.

Credible conformation and stereochemical identity of the small-ring fusions and the aromatic-labelled large nitrogen ring are unresolved. Aromatic perception alone does not establish a stable aromatic conformation.
Independent feasible arrangements at comparable scores remain limited. The data do not identify a required absent amine, stereoisomer or target-specific heterocycle.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted dione scores 0.0020944534688323298. A 60-heavy-atom coupled polycyclic dione at seed 0 evaluation 21 scores 8.256363320677636e-50, while fluorine gas at seed 2 evaluation 159 scores 4.97400031457045e-24; neither size nor fluorine alone supplies the favorable arrangement. The seed-2 expanded-ring leader scores 0.5383038522927281, and a related fused bicyclic dione at evaluation 191 scores 0.5306138222816477, so the expanded ring is not the only observed topology with substantial reward. Adding a methyl branch to the leader's fluoroacetyl group at evaluation 297 reduces the score to 0.3238267097449548; the further aryl-fluorinated final molecule at evaluation 300 scores 0.2138626024774967. This local comparison supports sensitivity to substituent composition and arrangement, not a monotonic reward for more fluorine or greater elaboration. Child best observed scores on seeds 0, 1 and 2 are 0.42137887667973745, 0.5293180188800544, 0.5383038522927281; the published Parent values in the same order are 0.6510211907030741, 0.4870057305679067, 0.7208853668418119. The better Child seed-1 result and lower other seed results coexist with different chemical liabilities; no specific reactive bond or missing drug-like motif is established as causal.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original gap source: n-c55c3d520a2c, carried into n-62daf219c70a; re-observed in n-ee95752352ec on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the supplied epoch-1 profile, batch size 10 and 300 observations per trajectory. The fluorinated dione output contains N-halogen bonds in 700 of 870 proposals, while the extensively decorated nitrogen-rich aromatic family contains O-halogen bonds in 224 of 870. A comparatively conventional nitrile/benzyl-ketone leader and recognizable aryl cyclic amines are counterexamples: feasible functional groups are available, and the problem is environment-specific. A hydroxyl analogue scores above its closely related O-F replacement in another family.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bonding when elaborating otherwise useful aromatic and polar frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide bond-environment-aware alternatives that preserve favorable combinations learned from task-local feedback while offering ordinary nitrogen substitution, carbon-bound halogens and stable oxygen connectivity. Assess those alternatives rather than assuming a universal heteroatom or halogen filter improves score. This association does not identify a responsible search component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original gap source: n-c55c3d520a2c, carried into n-62daf219c70a; re-observed in n-ee95752352ec on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the supplied epoch-1 profile, batch size 10 and 300 observations per trajectory. Current leaders include an N-N-containing four-membered thione fusion, an oxygen-containing four-membered fusion, cyclopropene-containing polycycles, medium-ring bridges and an aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen ring. The Parent small cyclic cumulene is a different historical manifestation; it is not claimed as the current leading motif. Ordinary azetidine and pyrrolidine units and less elaborated high-scoring relatives prevent treating all small rings or ring formation as pathological.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator can construct valid ring graphs without establishing credible geometry for their complete unsaturation and fusion patterns.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent ring-size, bond-geometry and junction constraints when proposing feasible alternative connectivities around learned functional-group relationships. Parsed valence, aromatic labels and additional ring counts cannot substitute for geometric assessment. Any score benefit from such constraints remains to be tested independently.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original gap source: n-c55c3d520a2c, carried into n-62daf219c70a; re-observed in n-ee95752352ec on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the supplied epoch-1 profile, batch size 10 and 300 observations per trajectory. Every supplied Child task has stereocentre-string incidence 0.0, while the aryl-amine, bridged dicarbonyl and fluorinated polycycle examples contain unassigned potential centres. The nitrile/benzyl-ketone leader does not require the same tetrahedral assignments. Formal-charge incidence is separately 0.0 despite the presence of basic aliphatic amines.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks defined stereochemical identity after generating potentially stereogenic saturated centres and ring junctions.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or deliberately resolve stereochemical identity when the generated connectivity requires it, distinguishing potential centres from configurationally stable stereoisomers. Treat protonation, tautomerism and alkene geometry as separate representation questions. These records establish unspecified identity, not a measured stereochemical score penalty.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original gap source: n-c55c3d520a2c, carried into n-62daf219c70a; re-observed in n-ee95752352ec on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the supplied epoch-1 profile, batch size 10 and 300 observations per trajectory. The scored output includes isolated halogens and small hydrocarbons at observed floors as well as very large coupled aromatic proposals with poor scores. The extended dione family has median 41 heavy atoms versus its Parent's 33 and leaders with 48, 50 and 57 heavy atoms, yet peripheral modifications often tie. A compact conventional ketone and less elaborated aryl-amine or nitrogen-carbonyl relatives show that useful smaller chemistry is already possible.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve useful chemical context while avoiding excessive fragmentation and elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use task-local evidence to preserve jointly useful functional regions while testing simplification or replacement of dispensable pieces. Context-preserving changes should remain available alongside scaffold reorganization. Neither a universal minimum size nor a general preference for larger molecules follows from these observations.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original gap source: n-c55c3d520a2c, carried into n-62daf219c70a; re-observed in n-ee95752352ec on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the supplied epoch-1 profile, batch size 10 and 300 observations per trajectory. Leading neighborhoods repeatedly retain nitrile fused-heterocycle/carbonyl, decorated dione, aryl-amine or bridged nitrogen-carbonyl organizations while changing short substituents, halogen placement or ring segments. Different seeds do reach different families, and some nearby topology alternatives keep comparable scores. The evidence therefore supports uneven coverage of useful feasible alternatives, not global structural collapse or inability to form rings.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently produce independent plausible alternatives to the leading scaffold family within each seed.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer chemically independent connectivities that preserve the favorable functional-group relationships learned from accepted observations, and verify their feasibility and actual scores. New strings or additional rings alone cannot demonstrate useful coverage. These chemical associations neither attribute convergence to a component nor establish that diversity allocation improves endpoints.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
